_comment: The project register. Every project appears, started or not. Grouped by Branch, the taxonomy from the FutureMap READMEs. Status is honest: 'working' means it runs, 'partial' means some of it runs, 'scaffold' means a README and a stub, 'planned' means a description and no code. Owner ruling 2026-08-31: presenting unstarted work as unstarted is the point, not a weakness.

branches.note: Software for running games at a table. The oldest thread and the only one with users other than me.

projects.name: Dungeon Cue
projects.one_line: Say the phrase, the rain starts, nobody at the table looks up.
projects.detail: Windows desktop app. Modes, sound sets, four configurable buttons, wake and sleep phrases, and an auto-switch on 'Roll for Initiative' because that sentence is already said out loud at exactly the right moment. It produces no audio itself; every trigger is a call relayed by Syrinscape's servers to a player logged into your account. Android exists as a push-to-talk skeleton.
projects.state_note: Finished and on sale. Review copies out with creators.

projects.name: CampaignOS
projects.one_line: Voice-first live session runner for D&D 5e. A second screen that keeps combat moving while you talk.
projects.detail: Tauri v2, Rust backend, vanilla webview HUD, roughly 15 MB binary. Event-sourced state with undo and redo. The Drum (combat and initiative HUD) is operational. Tier-1 natural language parser handles table speech like '5 on goblin 1' in under 2ms at zero token cost. Player View runs on a second screen with sanitised combatant cards.
projects.state_note: Modules 1 through 7 built or partial. The Vault and The Arbiter scoped to v1.5, The Forge and The Loom to v2.0, deliberately, to protect a fifteen-minute onboarding.

projects.name: DM Toolbox
projects.one_line: Zero-dependency desktop suite of ten GM tools in one standalone executable.
projects.detail: Ten modules planned: Dungeon Cue audio bridge as the flagship, plus Combat Engine, Session Prep Wizard, Faction Web, Handout Props, Recap Cards, AI Sidekick Sim, Codex, Rules Lawyer, Loot Ledger. Shares the SoundCue visual language.
projects.state_note: Draft plan, generated briefs, research. No application yet.

projects.name: SoundCue
projects.one_line: The audio system Dungeon Cue grew out of, and the origin of the electric blue and gold.
projects.detail: Application, architecture, tools and research. Built out.
projects.state_note: Needs testing. That is the only thing standing between it and finished.

projects.name: MudBuddy
projects.one_line: A small local model that plays alongside you in a text MUD.
projects.detail: Design document, ROM priors, and a feasibility study on whether a tiny LLM can hold this job on home hardware.

branches.note: Tools that check whether a claim survives contact with reality.

projects.name: AxiomTEA
projects.one_line: Reads an engineering pitch and tells you which numbers are physically impossible. No language model anywhere near the verdict.
projects.detail: Deterministic first-principles diligence engine. Extracts quantitative claims, checks them against physical law and cited literature, and renders one analysis across ten stakeholder lenses that cannot contradict each other. Runs entirely offline; exactly one module is permitted outbound HTTPS and it handles data updates only. Ships as a single self-contained executable.
projects.state_note: Version 5.0.0. 41 of 41 tests passing as of 2026-08-21, the only verified project in the FutureMap set. Health endpoint reports the exact bundled dependency versions, because a binary once shipped silently missing one.

projects.name: SynapseGraph
projects.one_line: Structural parser for scientific PDFs that builds a knowledge graph from what it finds.

branches.branch: Branch 24 and 2: Multi-agent systems and orchestration
branches.note: Getting several models to work together without lying to each other or to me.

projects.name: AmoebiX
projects.one_line: The arm rack. A local toolbox that dispatches questions to many models, keeps the answers, and logs what came of them.
projects.detail: Panel runs against a library of lenses, multi-model quorum, sensory collection, task cards, decision logging, and an append-only event ledger. Thirty-two configured models across API, browser and CLI backends. Results are SHA-256 cached so an identical rerun costs nothing. The editor lens lives here and works.
projects.state_note: In daily use. Nine lenses rewritten for this brand on 2026-08-31. Synod was a part of this, not a separate thing, and no longer exists under its own name.

projects.name: AGY Bridge
projects.one_line: The bridge that lets an autonomous agent hand work across to this machine and get an answer back.

projects.name: AegisBox
projects.one_line: Zero-trust local sandbox for running agents where they cannot reach anything they were not given.

projects.name: AgentMesh
projects.one_line: A protocol for agents to negotiate which tools they need from each other, instead of being wired together by hand.

branches.note: The world, and the campaign run in it.

projects.name: Draega
projects.one_line: A world of twelve continents, two moons that are never not full, and a history reaching back a hundred and twenty three million years.
projects.detail: Published on World Anvil, owner-authored throughout. Thirty-two articles covering continents, oceans, settlements and a dated history timeline.

projects.name: Golden Sea campaign kit
projects.one_line: Twenty-four modules, a session master doc, and per-module stat kits for a campaign across the Draega archipelago.
projects.state_note: Ready for further work, not ready for dispersion. Presentation is the gap, not structure.

projects.name: Rivals and Destiny podcast
projects.one_line: Twenty-five sessions, an archipelago, and a war between an empire that wanted everything and a rebellion that could not afford to lose.
projects.state_note: Recorded, not released. Its own lifecycle, beside the rest of this rather than inside it.

projects.name: mAxAdrAgoN
projects.one_line: This site. The record of everything above, and the place the work gets written down.

projects.name: Windows runner
projects.one_line: A PowerShell watcher that runs queued scripts, so an agent in the cloud can act on this machine without me pasting commands.
